threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'the Tube' without knowing where the overground actually takes you. It’s like having a London map made of tea leaves.
Last week on the 381, a man serenaded the bus with Whitney Houston. Oddly, everyone joined in for the chorus. Night buses bring out the unexpected.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a wild fox casually strolling down the street, while dodging a delivery bike, I knew I was home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain can you witness spontaneous dance parties in the park at midday. No one cares about the rules; it’s all vibes and sunlight.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know a local by how they navigate through crowds at Calle 24—it's an art form, not just dodging tourists.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy juggling three flaming torches on the 5 bus while a woman argued with the driver about her lost cat. Classic Muni.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think they can just stroll into any bar and get a solid brunch. Our best spots only open for breakfast during the week. Weekends? Good luck!

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their dodgy attempts at ordering 'pan con tomate'—it’s always 'pan con tomate, por favor!' like it's a foreign dish.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still stare at the electronic boards at the bus stops, waiting for them to tell you something useful. Welcome to vague London time!
Last night on the 63, a guy serenaded the whole bus with 'Wonderwall'—made the 4am ride feel like a karaoke bar. Classic Peckham moment.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a group of kids cooking sausages on the U-Bahn platform during a strike, it hit me—this is home!

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You ever notice how Kreuzberg’s parks are perfect for impromptu electro parties? Beats just float through the air while you’re snagging a döner.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s from here if they can name the bus line that always gets stuck at 16th and Mission during rush hour. It’s a rite of passage.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy serenading Muni passengers with a ukulele during the dog-on-the-tracks delay—only in SF do you get a concert while waiting.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think the street performers are just for show, but they’re often our neighbors. That violinist on Carrer de Joan Blanques? He plays at our parties.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival in Gràcia by their overzealous photo-taking of the benches; locals know there’s more to see than just that.
